decisions.decision: Resume RM24 in artifacts-only mode: create and commit the tier-3 OpenSpec artifacts, then checkpoint before any implementation wave
decisions.why: The 5-hour bucket had not reset at resume (77% vs the 90 threshold, resets ~14:00 UTC) and tier 2 alone consumed ~36 points, so a full tier-3 run was projected to trip the gate mid-sweep. The leader presented artifacts-only / full-autopilot / wait-for-reset; the user chose artifacts-only, which is cheap (one dispatch) and lets the implementation waves start on a clean bucket.

decisions.decision: Leader-amended design.md D1 and tasks.md T14.1 at artifact reconcile: pass 1 of i18n-guard must match the i18n:allow marker on the PRECEDING line for .templ files, not line-locally; added T14.1b to prove the hatch fires
decisions.why: As authored, D1 placed the marker on the preceding line for .templ (correct - templ has no in-markup comment syntax and CLAUDE.md forbids HTML comments) but specified the guard skips lines CONTAINING the marker. The escape hatch would have been inert, and T14.3 forbids relaxing the pattern - leaving a worker stuck. Fixing at reconcile costs pennies vs a review round plus rework wave (Step 5.6).

decisions.decision: Seeded progress.json tasks[] at GROUP granularity (T1-T17) rather than tier 2's sub-task granularity (T1.1, T1.2, ...)
decisions.why: design.md D4 makes the group the actual dispatch and parallelism unit - dependencies are declared group-to-group, and 60+ sub-task entries would be re-read by the leader at every wave boundary for no added truth. tasks.md keeps sub-task-level checkboxes, and per the skill's guardrail tasks.md wins on implementation done-ness.

decisions.decision: Database design gate cleared without a user confirmation round
decisions.why: The gate is blocking only when a gated area is touched. design.md states explicitly that this tier changes no schema, migration, sqlc query, table, column, or index, and the leader verified that against the proposal's impact list (templates, handlers, catalog.go, Makefile, docs). There is no design for the user to confirm.

decisions.decision: Serialized T11 behind T9 (was: both depends_on [T1], both parallel_ok) because T9.3 and T11 both edit internal/gateway/handlers/handlers.go
decisions.why: design.md D4 asserts every group from T2 onward touches a disjoint file, and serializes catalog.go for exactly this reason - but it missed that its own T9.3 (relativeLastSeen) lands in handlers.go alongside all of T11. Dispatching them as a parallel wave would reproduce the merge collision D4 exists to prevent. Cost of the fix at reconcile: one dependency edge. Cost if found later: a corrupted wave and a rework round.
